photo.title: Dancers dressed elaborately as mythological birds at funeral (coffin is seen in background).
Shan woman wearing pale top and characteristic Shan head-cloth (black, with striping and panels of geometric patterns in colours).

Part of the official enthronement ceremony for a Sawbwa. The Sawbwa sits on an elaborate throne embellished with mythological lion and other figures. Offerings in lacquered and other vessels sit on the floor in front of him. Also in front of him seven men sit on the floor. They are evidently elders, and all but one are quite planly dressed. The other wears ornate ceremonial clothes, including a pointed minister's hat. The Sawbwa himself wears elaborate ceremonial royal dress (not the same as he wears in 1998.312.701.1), including a headdress and ornate, flanged coat.

Part of the official enthronement ceremony for a Sawbwa. The Sawbwa, in ornate ceremonial clothes, sits on an elaborate throne on a dais to right of picture. Main image consists of a row of monks, all painted pink (image intensifier?), and in front of them in an attitude of obeisance is a woman.
Portrait of a man in the street wearing floppy hat and carrying bundles under his arm, cigar in the other.

Part of the official enthronement ceremony for a Sawbwa. The Sawbwa and his wife (Mahadevi) sit on elaborate thrones embellished with mythological lion and other figures. Large decorated parasols shade them. They wear ceremonial dress. The Sawbwa wears a long ?brocade coat buttoned down the front with a mandarin collar, wide trousers, shoes with a bow on the front, and an ornamented turban. He also wears glasses. His wife wears an embroidered skirt-cloth (htamein) and elaborately embroidered shoulder and breast cloths, with a plain jacket. She holds something large and feathery (?a boa) on her lap.

Part of the official enthronement ceremony for a Sawbwa. A procession of people leave a thatched roofed structure standing in water via a bridge. Parasols are carried over the two (male and female?) figures at the front (Sawbwa and his wife?).
Shan women in Lashio market selling ?bean cakes from large baskets.
Funeral juggernaut as part of the procession at Byan (funeral) of 'Rural Dean', decorated with paintings, flags, white silk umbrellas and pagoda-like structures.  Spectators to left of juggernaut.
Boy dressed, ornamented and made-up for shinpyu (shinbyu) festival (ritual initiation into the monkhood).
Shan woman wearing pale top and characteristic Shan head-cloth (black, with striping and panels of geometric patterns in colours). She also wears ear studs.

Part of the official enthronement ceremony for a Sawbwa. Three daughters of the Sawbwa (?) flanked each side by another little girl, more plainly dressed. The middle girl of the five stands, and those immediately each side of her sit on ornate chairs. These three wear elaborate headdreses, long embroidered coats, Shan style open skirt cloths (htamein), and neck ornaments.

Part of the official enthronement ceremony for a Sawbwa. Senior men sit and stand behind a ?table, one operating a chain that seems to be part of a pulley system on the end of which appears to be a large pair of scissors.

Shan Tayok man standing in front of carved panel screen (?of monastery), behind two small boys dressed up for shinpyu [shinbyu] festival, as a result of which they will enter monkhood for a brief period. Other boys stand to side.
